name: Showering twice daily
lead: Showering twice daily is a hygiene routine, usually morning and evening or after exercise, adopted in appearance-focused communities to control body odour and keep skin and hair clean. Personal hygiene is generally described as cleanliness practices for health and social acceptance, and norms vary by culture and era.[1]
No published trial comparing twice-daily showering with once-daily showering for appearance or odour was found in the sources consulted.

paras: Regular bathing is an old practice; Roman civilisation is noted for it, and Han-dynasty officials were required to bathe every five days.[1] Modern advice and expectations differ between cultures and over time.[1]

Proponents treat frequent showering as a baseline for grooming and scent, often alongside deodorant and fragrance. Some people also describe skin dryness as a concern with frequent washing; the general hygiene reference consulted does not address this.

lore.intro: Twice-daily showering is discussed as a grooming baseline.

claims.claim: Showering twice a day improves smell and skin presentation
claims.believers: Proponents say it removes sweat and oil before they cause odour or shine.
claims.experts: No published studies were found testing this routine for appearance outcomes.

card.summary: Morning and evening showers for odour control; common habit, no studies on the twice-daily part.
card.note: Some people report skin dryness; unstudied here.

quick.overview:
Showering twice daily means washing in the morning and again later, often after exercise or before going out.

It is a grooming baseline in appearance communities.
quick.mechanism: Washing removes sweat, oil and surface bacteria that contribute to odour.
quick.risks: No documented harms were found in the sources consulted; skin dryness is a concern some people raise.
